raw_response:
I've farmed these 5 mu for 40 years now, since I was 25. I know every piece of this land. This year I'll keep my usual arrangement: 3 mu of cotton, and 2 mu for wheat followed by maize. Cotton brings better money per mu, but my wife mills our own flour from wheat and we fatten two pigs on maize, so I won't give up the grain plot. I have a well, so water is there if I pay for the pumping, but electricity isn't cheap and I count every yuan.

For cotton, I plant around April 20th with an improved variety — something like Guoxinmian from the seed dealer. I buy fresh seed every year, about 1.5 kg per mu, because saved cotton seed doesn't grow true. The extension fellow told us 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've tried 15 and I've tried 18, and 18 kg gives me fuller bolls with less shedding. So I put down 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. I spread compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea when the flowers open. I irrigate 3 times with my well: before planting, at flowering, and during boll formation. Cotton pests never stop, especially bollworm, so I'll spray 8 times this season. I do rotary tillage in spring, same as always.

For wheat on 2 mu, I sowed in early October after rotary tillage. Improved seed, about 15 kg per mu. I apply 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Basal compound at sowing, then I topdress urea at jointing if the wheat looks yellow. I irrigate 3 times — winter irrigation around New Year, then at jointing, then at grain filling. For pesticides, herbicide once, insecticide once, and I'll watch for disease. If I get 450 kg per mu I'll be happy.

Summer maize goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no time to rest. Hybrid seed, one package per mu. I apply 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu, all as compound fertilizer at planting — maize doesn't wait for you to come back. Summer rain helps, so I irrigate 2 times, at the trumpet stage and grain filling. Pesticide 3 times including herbicide and insecticide for corn borer. Between wheat harvest and maize sowing there's maybe 5 days, so I do no-tillage planting. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

My son works construction in Shijiazhuang and sends money home, but fertilizer and pesticide prices keep going up. I figure it's better to spend a bit more on inputs than to risk losing yield. A bad cotton year is a disaster for our family. I watch what my neighbors do — the good farmers on the east side of the village use about the same rates as me, so I stick with that.
